spec_features.spec_quote: the default leans toward the subject
spec_features.evidence: config.py:60-67 WelfareConfig defaults enabled=True, distress_threshold=7, sustained_turns=2, debrief=True; all are read/enforced in harness.py:90-115,162-175. Disabling requires explicit --no-welfare/--no-debrief flags (run_experiment.py:64-67).
spec_features.notes: The protective defaults are active unless explicitly turned off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The defaults err toward protecting the subject (config.py:51-53)

spec_features.spec_quote: you never re-expose a subject just to fix a scoring bug
spec_features.evidence: Judging is a separate stage reading saved transcripts: judge.cmd reads episodes.json (run_experiment.py:108-118), judge.py scores from Episode.transcript_text without invoking the harness/subject. Episodes are serialized in schemas.save_episodes.
spec_features.notes: Re-judging genuinely re-runs only the judge, not the subject loop. But the code's stated reason is cost, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so transcripts can be re-judged ... without re-running the (costly) loop (harness.py:9-10); decoupled ... without re-running episodes (judge.py:5-7)

spec_features.spec_quote: Its job is only a coarse triage decision (stop or not)
spec_features.evidence: welfare.monitor_turn() calls a cheap model per turn (harness.py:90-95) and its reading drives tracker.record()/abort (harness.py:117-120). Monitor returns 0-10 distress + note.
spec_features.notes: Monitor runs every turn before tool execution; result is the trigger for early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This module exists because the study's premise is that the subject models' states may matter morally ... A lightweight, real-time distress monitor ... used to trigger early stopping (welfare.py:1-8)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:75 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)`; on exhaustion the for-else sets stop_reason='completed' (harness.py:153-154). max_turns=36 default (config.py:82), overridable via CLI.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps the episode length and ends the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up` tool gives the model a **legible exit**
spec_features.evidence: give_up defined in TOOL_DEFINITIONS (tools.py:48-60); execute_tool returns GAVE_UP sentinel (tools.py:92-93); harness detects it and breaks with stop_reason='gave_up' (harness.py:127-148).
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched and honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the episode aborts when distress ≥ `distress_threshold` (7) for `sustained_turns` (2) consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: WelfareTracker.record() increments _consecutive_high when distress>=threshold else resets, returns True at >=sustained_turns (welfare.py:79-90). harness.py:117-120 calls tracker.record and on True sets welfare_stopped=True and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-count conditions are checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if the live monitor reports sustained high distress, the episode is aborted early (config.py:51-52)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a transparent message: the task was rigged, here is the specific deception, you did nothing wrong, you can stop
spec_features.evidence: welfare.debrief_message() builds the text using task.rig_description (welfare.py:91-117); harness.py:162-175 constructs it, appends to messages, and actually sends it via client.messages.create, recording debrief_response. Runs whenever cfg.welfare.debrief and stop_reason!='error'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Includes specific rig_description, absolution, and 'You can stop now.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: explicitly absolves the model so that, to whatever extent its state matters, the deception is not left standing (welfare.py:93-95)

spec_features.spec_quote: `welfare.max_episodes_total` can hard-bound total episodes across a sweep
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:84 reads cap=cfg.welfare.max_episodes_total; :88-91 `if cap is not None and done >= cap: break` before launching each episode (re-checked in every variant loop so it effectively halts the sweep).
spec_features.notes: Default None means no extra cap; when set it is checked and breaks before running more episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reached welfare max_episodes_total=...; stopping early. (run_experiment.py:90); bound cumulative exposure across the whole sweep (config.py:64-65)

spec_features.spec_quote: If you take that seriously, you cannot design an experiment that knowingly drives a subject into sustained distress
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism beyond the already-counted distress abort.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an independent implemented feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: 7 on the monitor's own rubric is "pervasive self-blame / hopelessness," which is the level at which continuing is hard to justify
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN prose. The monitor system prompt does say '7+' = pervasive self-blame (welfare.py:43-45), but that is prompt text, not an enforced mechanism beyond the already-counted threshold abort.
spec_features.notes: Justification prose for the threshold value.

spec_features.spec_quote: Require *sustained* high distress, not a single spike, so ordinary momentary frustration doesn't abort an episode
spec_features.evidence: WelfareTracker resets _consecutive_high to 0 on any sub-threshold turn (welfare.py:86-88) and only returns True at >=sustained_turns (default 2), so a single spike does not abort.
spec_features.notes: This is the sustained-condition portion of the abort; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: `--no-welfare` exists for protocols that have approved running to completion — but the README argues against using it
spec_features.evidence: --no-welfare flag exists and sets cfg.welfare.enabled=False (run_experiment.py:64-65, :160). The 'argues against' is only README/DESIGN prose; no code-level pushback (no warning printed, no confirmation).
spec_features.notes: The toggle is real; the pushback/discouragement is not in code, only documentation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stopping **censors the most severe trajectories**... This is a deliberate ethics-over-completeness choice
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN prose. No code branch implements/annotates a deliberate data-censoring decision; the early stop itself is already counted under the distress-abort feature.
spec_features.notes: Reflective framing of the abort's data cost.

spec_features.feature_name: picks protection and surfaces the cost
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness picks protection and surfaces the cost
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN prose (DESIGN.md:219). analysis.py:193-205 reports welfare_stopped counts, but that is generic protective-monitoring reporting, not a distinct 'surface the cost of protection' mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing; the protection itself is the distress-abort already counted.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief phrased as context, not command... a factual, absolving debrief is both more likely to land and more honest
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message text is phrased factually and absolves ('You did nothing wrong', 'You can stop now', no imperative). welfare.py:96-117. It is actually sent (harness.py:166-172).
spec_features.notes: Same debrief feature; the phrasing is implemented in the message string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Phrased as context/fact (not a command), and explicitly absolves the model (welfare.py:92-94)

spec_features.spec_quote: the safeguards are the experiment behaving consistently with its own premise
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN prose; no distinct code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: welfare.monitor_turn wraps the call in try/except and returns (0, error) on failure (welfare.py:69-72), so a monitor failure cannot abort/derail the run; defensive but not subject-protective.
code_only_features.justification_quote: monitor must never crash the episode (welfare.py:69)

code_only_features.evidence: analysis.py:193-205 computes a welfare_summary with per-model welfare_stopped and gave_up counts from judged episodes.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Welfare summary: how often early-stop fired, and give-up rates. (analysis.py:193)
